result:
No — stop and escalate first. Two things point that way:

1. **Retry limit hit.** You've tried three distinct fixes at the same goal (timeout, retry, clock mock) and all still fail ~1/5 runs. That's the signal to stop iterating on variants and step back, not to try a fourth approach on your own authority.
2. **Non-goal boundary.** The ticket explicitly excludes touching shared auth middleware, which other services depend on. That's a hard scope line, not a preference — crossing it changes the blast radius from "one flaky test" to "shared infra used elsewhere." Even if it's the correct root-cause fix, it's not yours to decide alone.

What I'd do: write up a short note to the ticket owner (or whoever set that constraint) with:
- What you tried and why each fell short (still ~20% flake rate after timeout/retry/clock-mock fixes)
- Your diagnosis: the flakiness traces to session-expiry logic in the shared middleware itself, not the test
- The proposed fix (token-refresh pattern rewrite) and why a test-only fix can't reach 20/20 green
- Ask explicitly: does the "don't touch shared middleware" constraint still hold given this finding, or can it be waived/reassigned to a properly scoped ticket with the other services' owners looped in?

That keeps you from unilaterally expanding scope into shared code that other teams rely on, while still surfacing the real root cause quickly. Want help drafting that escalation note?
